transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Finch Legal. This is Jordan. What brings you in touch today?

transcript.text: Hi, I slipped at a neighborhood grocery store and my wrist still isn't right. I kept thinking it would settle down, but carrying shopping bags hurts.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: I'm sorry you've been dealing with that. Could I get your full legal name before we go through the details?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My full name is Elena Sofia Morales.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Tell me when and where it happened, and what you remember about the incident.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What injuries were diagnosed, and where did you receive care?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My sister drove me to Rosebridge Medical Center that evening. The diagnosis was a left wrist sprain and lumbar strain. They took X-rays and said there wasn't a fracture. I went home with a brace and instructions to follow up.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What treatment has happened since then, and how are you doing now?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I've done ten physical therapy visits at Maple Rehabilitation. My back is better, but twisting a jar open still sets off the wrist. They're talking about a referral if it doesn't improve after the next few visits.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: How has this affected your work and ordinary day-to-day activities?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm thirty-six and pack online orders at a small bookstore. I missed nine shifts, then went back on shorter hours. My manager can print the schedule changes; I don't have a final lost-wage number yet.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Do you have an approximate total for medical charges so far?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The statements I have total about $5,600. That's the billed amount, not necessarily what I personally owe. Some insurance adjustments haven't come through yet.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Were there earlier injuries or conditions we should know about? Have you hired another attorney?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I sprained that wrist playing volleyball in college, but hadn't needed treatment for years. No previous injury claim and no other attorney on this one.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What insurance information have you received, and has anyone confirmed coverage?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I used my own health insurance. The store manager said someone from their insurer would call, but nobody has told me the carrier or claim number. I haven't signed anything.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Were there witnesses, a report, or any other evidence that might help establish what happened?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: An employee named Owen Price helped me up. He told me he'd mentioned the leak that morning. I didn't record him, but he wrote his name on the incident slip. I have no idea whether he'll remember me.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What documents or photographs have you been able to keep?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I have a photo of the puddle, the incident slip, discharge papers, and my therapy receipts. The manager said there are cameras near the flowers. I'd really like someone to ask for that footage.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What is your main question or concern for the attorney who reviews this?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm worried waiting a few weeks made it look like nothing happened. I just couldn't afford to keep leaving work for appointments.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: I'll include that in the review. What phone number and email should we use for follow-up?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: You can reach me at 202-555-0100, and my email is elena.morales@example.com. A voicemail is fine if I'm at an appointment.

transcript.text: Let me check the basics: Elena Sofia Morales, an incident on April 19, 2025 at Cedar Basket Market, Maple Avenue, Portland. We'll review the records you've described and identify what's still missing. Did I get the date and place right?

transcript.text: Yes, that's right. Please send the document list by email so I can work through it without forgetting anything.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. I'll send the checklist and pass your account to the review team. They'll follow up about the open questions before any decision about representation.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I tripped on a raised section of a city path and tore ligaments in my ankle. Someone mentioned special paperwork for a city claim and I don't know where to start.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My full name is Megan Claire Sullivan.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Tell me when and where it happened, and what you remember about the incident.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: April 12, 2025, on Riverside Greenway near the boat launch in Boise. A concrete slab was raised where a tree root had pushed it up. My shoe caught the edge and I fell forward. There wasn't a cone or paint marking the change in height.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What injuries were diagnosed, and where did you receive care?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Foothill Community Hospital checked me that afternoon. The MRI later showed a grade three ankle sprain with an ATFL tear. I wore a boot for four weeks and then switched to a brace.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What treatment has happened since then, and how are you doing now?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Greenway Physical Therapy has seen me eight times. The ankle still gives way on uneven ground. The orthopedist mentioned possible reconstruction only if therapy fails; no surgery is scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: How has this affected your work and ordinary day-to-day activities?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm thirty-nine and run guided walking tours. I canceled three weekends and paid someone else to lead the rest. I have booking records and the substitute guide's invoices.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Do you have an approximate total for medical charges so far?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The statements I have total about $10,800. That's the billed amount, not necessarily what I personally owe. Some insurance adjustments haven't come through yet.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Were there earlier injuries or conditions we should know about? Have you hired another attorney?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I sprained the same ankle about ten years ago and had no symptoms before this. No other lawyer. I sent a message through the city's maintenance form but haven't filed any formal claim paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: What insurance information have you received, and has anyone confirmed coverage?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My own health plan has paid part of the treatment. I don't know if the city uses insurance or handles claims itself. The maintenance reply didn't identify a claims contact.

transcript.speaker: Intake Specialist
transcript.text: Were there witnesses, a report, or any other evidence that might help establish what happened?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: A jogger named Tessa Lane saw me fall and stayed until my partner arrived. She took a picture with a water bottle beside the raised edge for scale. I don't know how long the slab had been like that.
